Bristlecone v1.4.2 — weather learning and smoother Android updates

This one includes a fix for Android beta updates, along with the mountain-weather work from 1.4.1. I want you to be able to install the next beta without starting over. There is one awkward step if you already have an older Android build, so please read the backup note below before installing.

If you are coming from an earlier beta, here is what is in this build:

- **A trained temperature correction in Mountain weather.** It was trained on real station observations and runs on your phone alongside the physical weather model. The card also estimates wind, gusts, freezing levels, and rain or snow at your elevation and nearby high ground.
- **Several weather fixes.** Missing temperatures and snow levels no longer behave like zero readings. Temperature adjustments are counted once, the uncertainty range follows the age of the forecast, and a change at the edge of the learned model cannot pretend to be a freezing level.
- **A consistent signing key for Android release betas.** Starting with 1.4.2, future release betas using that key can update this version in place. The build now checks the selected key before building and verifies the finished APK too. Development builds are a separate channel.

The weather learning is still preliminary: 187 time-matched observations from 31 US stations, all from one October day. It applies only to supported October NWS forecasts within narrow training ranges, with terrain available and no overlapping station adjustment. Canada, other seasons, larger elevation differences and unsupported conditions use the physical model. Improvement on later hours was small; this is an early result, not broad validation of mountain-weather accuracy. The model is unchanged from 1.4.1. [The detailed notes](https://github.com/hayvenmjackson/bristlecone/releases/tag/v1.4.1) and [full evaluation](https://github.com/hayvenmjackson/bristlecone/blob/v1.4.1/tools/weather/evaluations/nws-pilot-2026-10-23.json) are there if you want to dig into it.

The other ML features are here too: Bristlecone learns your stride during clean GPS walks and hikes to help estimate movement when GPS drops out, and its trail-report filter learns from your feedback. These models run on your device. GPS-less positions are estimates from your last good fix, and weather estimates are not measurements. Keep an eye on landmarks, official forecasts and alerts, and the conditions in front of you.

**Already using Android 1.4.0 or 1.4.1? Please back up first.** Those builds used different temporary signing keys, so 1.4.2 cannot install over them. Export a Bristlecone backup and any important GPX tracks to private files outside the app, and check that the files actually saved. When you are ready, manually uninstall the old version, install 1.4.2, and restore your backup. Uninstalling removes app-local data, and some device-specific calibration is not included in backups and may need to be learned again. Bristlecone will not uninstall anything for you. This step does not apply to iOS.

Both downloads are attached below:

- [Android 8.0+ — APK](https://github.com/hayvenmjackson/bristlecone/releases/download/v1.4.2/Bristlecone-1.4.2-android.apk).
- [iPhone and iPad, iOS 16+ — unsigned IPA](https://github.com/hayvenmjackson/bristlecone/releases/download/v1.4.2/Bristlecone-1.4.2-ios-unsigned.ipa). This still needs signing/sideloading through AltStore or SideStore; opening the file alone will not install it.

These are beta downloads, not App Store or Google Play releases. The [Bristlecone page](https://krummholz.ai/apps/bristlecone/) now has more detail about the app, screenshots, and what the AI is doing.
